extractor.note: A sorge record already exists for this commentary. Under this theme the course's terms are Greek - aidion, aei, aion, kairos read as Augenblick - not Zeitlichkeit.

coverage_note: § 6 a (the always-being as the object of episteme), § 11 b (the temporal character of the as-soon-as/then nexus) and § 23 c (the moment of vision against the aei). The eight other sections with term hits are not extracted.

units.claim: The object of knowing is determined in its being by a moment of time: the always-enduring characterizes it, and being means for the Greeks being-present, being-in-the-now.
units.quote: Now the striking result: this being is determined *in its being* by a moment of *time*. The always-enduring characterizes it.

units.claim: Aion is glossed as lifetime understood as full being-present, the allotted span of presence a living thing disposes over, and in a wider sense the duration of the world.
units.quote: αἰών means lifetime understood as full being-present — τὸν ἅπαντα αἰῶνα (*De Caelo* A, 9; 279b22); every living thing has its αἰών, its allotted span of being-present, the measure of presence it disposes over

units.claim: What is not in time is for Aristotle still temporal, determined out of time, the always-being being not in time because its infinite nows are not measurable.
units.quote: It is therefore *not* "supra-temporal" in our sense: what is not "in time" is, for Aristotle, still *temporal*, i.e. determined *out of* time — the ἀίδιον not-in-time being determined precisely by the ἄπειρον of its nows.

units.claim: The point said to govern the whole course is that beings are interpreted in their being out of time, the object of episteme being the always-being.
units.quote: The point to hold fast, and it governs the entire course: beings are interpreted *in their being out of time*.

units.claim: The nexus of experience is called a purely temporal one, a peculiar nexus of the temporal being of Dasein in which making-present expresses itself as an as-soon-as.
units.quote: This nexus is manifestly a *temporal* one, and at first a *purely* temporal one: as-soon-as… then… — a peculiar nexus of the *temporal being* of Dasein. Dasein's *making-present*, which expresses itself in the "now," appears here as an "as-soon-as"

units.claim: The temporal structure of experience is named the nexus of making-present: as soon as this is present, then that must be made present too.
units.quote: Heidegger names this temporal structure the *nexus of making-present* (*Zusammenhang des Gegenwärtigens*): as soon as this is present, then that must be procured, made present too.

units.claim: Phronesis is the catching-sight of the this-time of the momentary situation, the moment of vision, against the regarding of what is always present in selfsameness.
units.quote: As αἴσθησις it is the *glance of the eye* — the *Augenblick*, the moment-of-vision — upon the respective concrete, which as such *can always be otherwise*. Whereas the νοεῖν in σοφία is the regarding of what is *ἀεί*, what is always present *in selfsameness*.

units.claim: Time - the moment of vision and the always-being - is said to function as the discrimen between the perceiving in phronesis and in sophia.
units.quote: **Time — the moment-of-vision and the always-being — functions here as the *discrimen* of the νοεῖν in φρόνησις and σοφία.**
